mean: to put a finger right on the crux of the matter
lit: one jab of the needle and blood shows

use.how: Predicate or adverbial: 他的话一针见血；一针见血地指出问题。 Said of a remark or analysis that names the real problem in few words.

near.diff: 直言不讳 is about frankness, saying things bluntly; 一针见血 is about accuracy, hitting the very heart of the problem.

cue: After two hours of a meeting circling the problem, the intern says one sentence that names its real cause. How was her remark?

ctx.s: 他的评论{一针见血}，说到了问题的关键。
ctx.en: His comment was spot on; it went right to the heart of the problem.

ctx.s: 老师{一针见血}地指出了我作文里最大的问题。
ctx.en: The teacher pinpointed the biggest problem in my essay.

ctx.s: “你不是没时间，是不想做。”妈妈的话{一针见血}。
ctx.en: "It's not that you don't have time, you just don't want to do it." Mum hit the nail on the head.

ctx.s: 开了两个小时会，新来的实习生一句话就{一针见血}：问题出在价格上。
ctx.en: After a two-hour meeting, the new intern nailed it in one sentence: the problem was the price.

ctx.s: 这篇书评写得{一针见血}，把小说最大的毛病说透了。
ctx.en: The review is razor-sharp; it lays bare the novel's biggest flaw.

ctx.s: 能{一针见血}地看出问题所在，是一个好经理必备的本领。
ctx.en: Being able to see straight to the core of a problem is a skill every good manager needs.

bad.s: 他讲了三个小时，{一针见血}地分析了每一个细节。
bad.en: (meant: he analysed every detail thoroughly for three hours)
bad.why: It praises a short, sharp remark that hits the key point, not a long, exhaustive analysis of every detail.

bad.s: 他{一针见血}地骂了我一顿，我很伤心。
bad.en: (meant: he scolded me cruelly and hurt me)
bad.why: It praises insight into the crux of a matter; it does not mean hurtful or harsh words.

mean: too complicated or painful to sum up in a few words
lit: hard to say it all in one word

use.how: Predicate, often as a sighing reply: 唉，一言难尽。 Said of one's own experiences or a tangled affair, hinting at hardship.

near.diff: 说来话长 only says the story is long to tell; 一言难尽 hints the matter is tangled or painful, often with a sigh.

cue: An old friend asks how your last three years went; there was a lost job, a divorce and a move, and you just sigh. What do you say?

ctx.s: “你最近怎么样？”他苦笑着摇摇头：“唉，{一言难尽}。”
ctx.en: "How have you been?" He gave a wry smile and shook his head: "Oh, where do I start."

ctx.s: 这几年的经历，真是{一言难尽}。
ctx.en: What I've been through these past few years is hard to put into words.

ctx.s: 那段婚姻带给她的痛苦，真是{一言难尽}。
ctx.en: The pain that marriage caused her is more than words can say.

ctx.s: 她创业的辛苦{一言难尽}，只有她自己知道。
ctx.en: The hardships of starting her business are beyond a few words; only she really knows.

ctx.s: 两家公司之间的恩怨{一言难尽}，我们改天再聊吧。
ctx.en: The history between those two companies is too tangled to explain now; let's talk another day.

ctx.s: 他望着窗外，叹了口气说：“这里面的事，{一言难尽}啊。”
ctx.en: He looked out of the window and sighed: "There's more to it than I can tell you."

bad.s: 他说话总是{一言难尽}，很啰嗦。
bad.en: (meant: he is always long-winded)
bad.why: It describes a matter too tangled to sum up, not a person who talks too much.

bad.s: 这家餐厅的菜好吃得{一言难尽}。
bad.en: (meant: the food is indescribably delicious)
bad.why: It hints at complication or hardship, never at delight beyond words.

mean: to tell everything in full, holding nothing back
lit: one, five; one, ten: counting off by fives, every item tallied

use.how: Adverbial before 说, 讲, 告诉 or 交代, often with 地: 他一五一十地说了。 Said of recounting what happened, in full and truthfully.

cue: After the vase broke, your little brother sat your mother down and told her exactly what happened, step by step, leaving nothing out. How did he tell her?

ctx.s: 他把事情的经过{一五一十}地告诉了我。
ctx.en: He told me exactly how it all happened, from start to finish.

ctx.s: 别着急，你{一五一十}地说，到底发生了什么？
ctx.en: Calm down and tell me everything: what actually happened?

ctx.s: 孩子回家后，把学校里的事{一五一十}讲给妈妈听。
ctx.en: When the child got home, he told his mother everything that had happened at school.

ctx.s: 面对警察，他把那天晚上看到的情况{一五一十}说了出来。
ctx.en: In front of the police, he recounted everything he had seen that night.

ctx.s: “你都跟老板说了？”“嗯，我{一五一十}全交代了。”
ctx.en: "You told the boss everything?" "Yes, I came clean about all of it."

ctx.s: 回到家，她把在医院听到的话{一五一十}地转告了丈夫。
ctx.en: When she got home, she passed on to her husband every word she had heard at the hospital.

bad.s: 这本书我{一五一十}地读完了。
bad.en: (meant: I read the book cover to cover)
bad.why: It is used for telling or reporting what happened in full, not for reading or doing something thoroughly.

bad.s: 他说话{一五一十}，很有条理。
bad.en: (meant: he speaks in an organised way)
bad.why: It is an adverbial for recounting a particular matter in full, not a description of someone's speaking style.

mean: with a dead-serious, earnest air (often comically so)
lit: as proper as a volume of the classics

use.how: Adverbial with 地 or attributive with 的: 一本正经地说；一本正经的样子。 Describes a person's serious manner, often comic against a trivial topic.

near.diff: 装模作样 says the manner is put on to fool people; 一本正经 just describes a serious, earnest manner, sincere or deadpan.

cue: Your friend tells an absurd made-up story with a perfectly straight face, and for a minute everyone believes him. How did he tell it?

ctx.s: 他{一本正经}地问我：“猫会不会做梦？”
ctx.en: He asked me in all seriousness: "Do cats dream?"

ctx.s: 看他那{一本正经}的样子，大家都忍不住笑了。
ctx.en: Seeing how solemn he looked, everyone burst out laughing.

ctx.s: 小女孩{一本正经}地给布娃娃上课。
ctx.en: The little girl was giving her dolls a lesson with the utmost seriousness.

ctx.s: 他{一本正经}地胡说八道，我们差点儿信了。
ctx.en: He talked complete nonsense with a perfectly straight face, and we almost believed him.

ctx.s: “你别笑，我是{一本正经}地跟你说这件事。”
ctx.en: "Don't laugh, I'm telling you this in all seriousness."

ctx.s: 主持人{一本正经}地宣布：“今天会议的主题是午饭吃什么。”
ctx.en: The host announced with a dead-serious face: "Today's meeting is about what to have for lunch."

bad.s: 他工作很{一本正经}，从来不出错。
bad.en: (meant: he is meticulous at work and never makes mistakes)
bad.why: It describes a serious manner or expression, not careful, accurate work.

bad.s: 这个会议很{一本正经}。
bad.en: (meant: the meeting is very formal)
bad.why: It describes a person's manner, not the formality of an event such as a meeting.

mean: having nothing at all to one's name
lit: there is not one thing that one has

use.how: Predicate or attributive: 我一无所有；一无所有的穷学生。 Said of a person or family with no money or possessions, sometimes of life without love or health.

near.diff: 倾家荡产 is the act of losing a whole fortune; 一无所有 is the state of having nothing, whether lost or never had.

cue: A man arrived in the city at nineteen with no money, no friends and no job. Describe what he had at that time.

ctx.s: 刚来北京的时候，我{一无所有}。
ctx.en: When I first came to Beijing, I had nothing.

ctx.s: 一场大火之后，他们家变得{一无所有}。
ctx.en: After the fire, their family was left with nothing.

ctx.s: 他从一个{一无所有}的穷学生，变成了公司老板。
ctx.en: He went from a penniless student to the boss of a company.

ctx.s: “你什么都没有，凭什么娶我女儿？”“我现在是{一无所有}，但我会努力的。”
ctx.en: "You have nothing; what makes you think you can marry my daughter?" "I have nothing now, but I'll work hard."

ctx.s: 就算{一无所有}，我们还有彼此。
ctx.en: Even if we have nothing, we still have each other.

ctx.s: 有人说，没有健康，再有钱也等于{一无所有}。
ctx.en: Some say that without your health, however rich you are, you really have nothing.

bad.s: 我对这件事{一无所有}。
bad.en: (meant: I know nothing about this)
bad.why: It is about possessions, not knowledge; knowing nothing about a matter takes the idiom ending in zhi, to know.

bad.s: 这个房间很{一无所有}。
bad.en: (meant: the room is very empty)
bad.why: It cannot take hen (very), and it says a person owns nothing, not that a place is empty.

mean: completely unaware of a matter or its facts
lit: there is not one thing that one knows

use.how: Predicate, usually 对……一无所知: 我对这件事一无所知。 Said of not knowing the facts of a matter, event or person.

near.diff: 一窍不通 is having no grasp of a skill or field, like music or computers; 一无所知 is not knowing the facts of a matter.

cue: Your company was sold last week, and you only found out today from the news; nobody had said a word to you. How much did you know before?

ctx.s: 我对这件事{一无所知}。
ctx.en: I know nothing about this.

ctx.s: 在看到新闻之前，他对公司被卖的事{一无所知}。
ctx.en: Until he saw the news, he had no idea the company had been sold.

ctx.s: “你知道他们要搬家吗？”“我{一无所知}，没人告诉我。”
ctx.en: "Did you know they're moving?" "I had no idea; nobody told me."

ctx.s: 我们对这个人的过去几乎{一无所知}。
ctx.en: We know almost nothing about this man's past.

ctx.s: 那个邻居说，他对那天晚上的事{一无所知}。
ctx.en: The neighbour said he knew nothing about what happened that night.

ctx.s: 很多人吃了几年的药，却对它的副作用{一无所知}，这很危险。
ctx.en: Many people take a medicine for years yet know nothing about its side effects, which is dangerous.

bad.s: 我{一无所知}这件事。
bad.en: (meant: I know nothing about this)
bad.why: It cannot take an object; the matter must come before it, introduced by dui (about).

bad.s: 他钢琴弹得{一无所知}。
bad.en: (meant: he can't play the piano at all)
bad.why: It is about not knowing facts, not lacking a skill, and cannot be a complement after de; having no skill at all calls for a different idiom.

mean: to feel like old friends at the first meeting
lit: meeting once, it is as if they were old acquaintances

use.how: Predicate, with two people as subject: 我们一见如故。 Said only of people meeting for the first time who instantly get on like old friends.

near.diff: 一见钟情 is falling in love at first sight; 一见如故 is instant friendship, a mutual feeling of old acquaintance.

cue: At a conference you meet a stranger who loves the same books and grew up in your hometown; within an hour you are talking like childhood friends. How did you two get on?

ctx.s: 我们俩{一见如故}，聊了一整晚。
ctx.en: We hit it off right away and talked all night.

ctx.s: 第一次见面，他们就{一见如故}，后来成了最好的朋友。
ctx.en: They clicked the first time they met and later became best friends.

ctx.s: “你们认识很久了吧？”“没有，上个月才认识，不过{一见如故}。”
ctx.en: "You must have known each other for ages." "No, we only met last month, but it felt like we'd always been friends."

ctx.s: 两位老人在公园里{一见如故}，从此每天一起下棋。
ctx.en: The two old men took to each other at once in the park, and from then on played chess together every day.

ctx.s: 她和新同事{一见如故}，很快就无话不谈。
ctx.en: She and her new colleague got on like old friends and were soon telling each other everything.

ctx.s: 在火车上和一位陌生人{一见如故}，是这次旅行最难忘的事。
ctx.en: Striking up an instant friendship with a stranger on the train was the most memorable part of the trip.

bad.s: 他对她{一见如故}，马上就爱上了她。
bad.en: (meant: he fell in love with her at first sight)
bad.why: It is about friendship felt by both sides; falling in love at first sight is a different idiom.

bad.s: 我们是老同学，十年没见了，今天{一见如故}。
bad.en: (meant: old classmates reunited felt as close as ever)
bad.why: It is only for people meeting for the first time; old friends meeting again are already old friends.

lit: every lift of a hand and every movement

use.how: Noun phrase, usually after a possessor: 他的一举一动。 Often the object of 注意, 关注, 盯着 or 模仿, about someone being watched or copied.

cue: On her first day, the new teacher feels the whole class watching how she walks, gestures and writes on the board. What of hers are they watching?

ctx.s: 孩子会模仿父母的{一举一动}。
ctx.en: Children copy their parents' every move.

ctx.s: 明星的{一举一动}都受到媒体的关注。
ctx.en: Everything a celebrity does is watched by the media.

ctx.s: 第一天上班，我觉得老板在注意我的{一举一动}。
ctx.en: On my first day at work, I felt the boss was watching my every move.

ctx.s: “你为什么总看着我？”“我在学你做菜，你的{一举一动}我都要记住。”
ctx.en: "Why do you keep watching me?" "I'm learning to cook from you; I need to remember every move you make."

ctx.s: 他的{一举一动}都很得体，看得出家教很好。
ctx.en: Everything he does is so proper; you can tell he was raised well.

ctx.s: 猫躲在沙发后面，紧紧盯着小鸟的{一举一动}。
ctx.en: The cat hid behind the sofa, tracking the little bird's every movement.

bad.s: 他{一举一动}地走进了教室。
bad.en: (meant: he walked into the classroom step by step)
bad.why: It is a noun phrase meaning someone's every action, not an adverbial describing how one moves.

bad.s: 这个计划我们要{一举一动}完成。
bad.en: (meant: we must finish the plan in one go)
bad.why: It means a person's every movement, not doing something in a single move; for that use a word meaning in one go.

use.how: Predicate or degree complement after 得: 考得一塌糊涂。 Says a result, situation or performance is hopelessly bad; also of crying uncontrollably.

near.diff: 乱七八糟 is about disorder and mess; 一塌糊涂 says something turned out hopelessly badly, not just untidily.

cue: You didn't study, the exam was hard, and when the results came back you had your worst score ever. How did you do?

ctx.s: 这次考试我考得{一塌糊涂}。
ctx.en: I made a complete mess of this exam.

ctx.s: 他把这次谈判搞得{一塌糊涂}，公司丢了最大的客户。
ctx.en: He made such a mess of the negotiations that the company lost its biggest client.

ctx.s: “比赛怎么样？”“别提了，我们输得{一塌糊涂}。”
ctx.en: "How was the match?" "Don't ask; we got thrashed."

ctx.s: 看到电影的结局，她哭得{一塌糊涂}。
ctx.en: At the end of the film, she cried her eyes out.

ctx.s: 新经理上任半年，公司的业绩就差得{一塌糊涂}。
ctx.en: Six months after the new manager arrived, the company's results were dreadful.

ctx.s: 我的发音{一塌糊涂}，老师听了直摇头。
ctx.en: My pronunciation is hopeless; the teacher just kept shaking her head.

bad.s: 他是一个{一塌糊涂}的人，总是忘记带钥匙。
bad.en: (meant: he is a scatterbrained person who always forgets his keys)
bad.why: It describes how badly something turned out, not a person's character; it cannot label someone as forgetful or careless.

bad.s: 他{一塌糊涂}了这个项目。
bad.en: (meant: he messed up the project)
bad.why: It is not a verb and cannot take an object; it goes after de, as in ba xiangmu gao de yitahutu (made a shambles of the project).

lit: not one word is sent out

use.how: Predicate or adverbial with 地: 他一言不发地走了。 Said of someone who stays silent on an occasion when they could or should speak.

near.diff: 哑口无言 is being left with no answer, usually after losing an argument; 一言不发 is simply keeping silent, often by choice.

cue: Throughout the whole family quarrel, your father sat in the corner drinking his tea and didn't say a single thing. What did he do?

ctx.s: 他坐在那里，{一言不发}。
ctx.en: He sat there without saying a word.

ctx.s: 整个会上，经理{一言不发}，只是听大家说。
ctx.en: The manager didn't say a word throughout the meeting; he just listened.

ctx.s: “你怎么{一言不发}？是不是不高兴了？”
ctx.en: "Why aren't you saying anything? Are you upset?"

ctx.s: 被老师批评以后，他{一言不发}地走出了教室。
ctx.en: After being told off by the teacher, he walked out of the classroom without a word.

ctx.s: 吃饭的时候，爸爸一直{一言不发}，气氛有点儿紧张。
ctx.en: Dad didn't say a word all through dinner, and the atmosphere was a bit tense.

ctx.s: 记者问了好几个问题，那位演员却{一言不发}，转身离开了。
ctx.en: The reporters asked several questions, but the actor said nothing, turned and walked away.

bad.s: 这个婴儿还小，{一言不发}。
bad.en: (meant: the baby is too young to talk)
bad.why: It implies choosing silence when one could speak; it is not for someone who cannot talk yet.

bad.s: 他{一言不发}地告诉我，他明天要走了。
bad.en: (meant: he quietly told me he was leaving tomorrow)
bad.why: It means saying not a single word, so it cannot describe the manner of telling someone something; for speaking softly use xiaosheng (quietly).
